title: Translated-chart hull of an integral split-torus extension
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A commutative group scheme over a base has multiplication, inverse and identity morphisms over that base satisfying the commutative group identities. Separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. A scheme over a field $k$ is geometrically connected if its base change to every field extension of $k$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]; a scheme over $S$ has geometrically connected fibres if its fibre over each point $s\in S$ is geometrically connected over the residue field $\kappa(s)$. Let $\mathcal H\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme with geometrically connected finite-type generic fibre $H$, and suppose $\mathcal H$ is a Néron lft-model of $H$. A Néron lft-model of a smooth separated $K$-group $V$ means a smooth separated $S$-group $\mathcal V$, with a specified generic group isomorphism $\mathcal V_K\simeq V$, such that restriction is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(X,\mathcal V)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_K(X_K,V)$ for every smooth $S$-scheme $X$ [def-pc-base-change, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. It is only locally of finite type; finite type additionally requires quasi-compactness [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $Q\subseteq\mathcal H$ be its open subgroup of fibrewise identity components [def-weil-open-immersion], and suppose $Q$ is of finite type. Let $B$ be a smooth separated commutative finite-type $S$-group scheme with geometrically connected fibres, supplied with an exact sequence $1\to\mathbf G_{m,S}^r\to B\to Q\to1$ of fppf sheaves, $r\geq0$ [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-fppf-site]. Here $\mathbf G_{m,S}=\operatorname{Spec}R[t,t^{-1}]$ with multiplication, and exact means identification with the scheme-theoretic kernel and local surjectivity in the fppf topology. Put $G=B_K$ and use the generic isomorphism $Q_K=H$. Assume $\operatorname{Hom}_{K\text{-grp}}(H,\mathbf G_{m,K})=0$. There exists a smooth separated commutative $S$-group scheme $N$, locally of finite type, with $N_K=G$ and an open group immersion $B\hookrightarrow N$ inducing the identity on generic fibres. Its image is $N^0$, the open subgroup of fibrewise identity components. If $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is a strict henselization [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] and $K^{\mathrm{sh}}=\operatorname{Frac}(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$, set $\Delta=G(K^{\mathrm{sh}})/B(R^{\mathrm{sh}})$, viewing integral sections as generic points. For representatives $a_\delta\in G(K^{\mathrm{sh}})$, $N_{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}$ is the gluing of copies $B_\delta$ of $B_{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}$ with their entire generic fibres identified with $G_{K^{\mathrm{sh}}}$ by $b\mapsto a_\delta b$; different copies have only that generic fibre as overlap. This glued group descends to $R$. For every local injective extension of discrete valuation rings $R\to A$ for which $A$ is the local ring at a point of a smooth $R$-scheme, restriction $N(A)\to G(\operatorname{Frac}A)$ is surjective. No completeness, excellence or residue-field perfection is assumed.

proof.text: Put $D=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $F=\operatorname{Frac}D$. By [lem-exc-affine-strict-local-ring-comparison] with $X=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ itself and a geometric point over the closed point whose separable closure is the chosen residue closure, $D$ is $R$-isomorphic to the pointed-neighbourhood strict henselization $\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{S,\bar s}$. Apply [lem-sc-strict-henselization-dvr] to it at the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$: $D$ is a DVR. By [lem-sfb-neron-strict-local-descent-base-change](i), $\mathcal H_D$ is a Néron lft-model of $H_F$ and its identity subgroup is $Q_D$. Thus the supplied extension $B_D\to Q_D$ has precisely the hypotheses of [lem-sfb-torus-integral-coset-specialization]. It gives valuative saturation of $B(D)\subset G(F)$ and surjectivity of the coset map for every essentially smooth local DVR extension of $D$. These assertions concern the integral group $B$, not just the split torus in its kernel.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 7 proof, local construction; Proposition 3 for base change

proof.text: Let $\Delta=G(F)/B(D)$ and choose $a_\delta$ with $a_0=1$. For $\delta\ne\epsilon$ set $U_{\delta\epsilon}=(B_\delta)_F$, and set $U_{\delta\delta}=B_\delta$. The transition on the generic overlap is $b\mapsto a_\epsilon^{-1}a_\delta b$. Its composite with the transition to $B_\zeta$ is $b\mapsto a_\zeta^{-1}a_\delta b$, so the cocycle and overlap conditions hold, including repeated indices. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-glue-schemes] to obtain a scheme $Z$ covered by these charts, with the asserted intersections. By [lem-sfb-valuatively-saturated-translate-gluing] and the saturation obtained in step 1, $Z/D$ is smooth separated and locally of finite type, with $Z_F=G_F$. This is the separation input; smoothness of individual charts alone would not imply it.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Example 5 and Proposition 7, generic gluing and separation

proof.text: Define the multiplication on $B_\delta\times_D B_\epsilon$ to land in $B_{\delta+\epsilon}$ by $(b,c)\mapsto u_{\delta\epsilon}bc$, where $u_{\delta\epsilon}=a_{\delta+\epsilon}^{-1}a_\delta a_\epsilon\in B(D)$ by the definition of the quotient. Define inverse on $B_\delta$ by $b\mapsto v_\delta b^{-1}$ in $B_{-\delta}$, where $v_\delta=a_{-\delta}^{-1}a_\delta^{-1}\in B(D)$, and use the identity section in $B_0$. On every overlap these formulas become multiplication, inverse and identity on $G_F$, so they glue. The group identities hold already as identities of these formulas on each product of charts: the correction factors telescope to the same product of representatives. Commutativity follows from commutativity of $B$ and the representatives in $G(F)$. Hence $Z$ is a commutative group with open identity chart $B_D$. Its special fibre is the disjoint union of copies of $B_{\kappa(D)}$, each geometrically connected, while its generic fibre is the geometrically connected $G_F$. Thus $Z^0=B_D$. Replacing $a_\delta$ by $a_\delta c_\delta$, $c_\delta\in B(D)$, gives a chart isomorphism $b\mapsto c_\delta^{-1}b$, so the construction has the prescribed description for any representatives.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 7, explicit group laws on translated charts

proof.text: Let $D\to A$ be a local injective extension of DVRs with $A$ a local ring of a smooth $D$-scheme, and put $L=\operatorname{Frac}A$. By [lem-sfb-torus-integral-coset-specialization](b), every $g\in G(L)$ is $a_\delta b$ for some $b\in B(A)$. Its $A$-point in the chart $B_\delta$ extends $g$. Apply [lem-sfb-neron-dvr-point-criterion] to the smooth separated group $Z$ of steps 2–3: it is a Néron lft-model of $G_F$. Apply [lem-sfb-neron-strict-local-descent-base-change](ii) to $V=G/K$ and this $Z/D$. It yields a smooth separated commutative Néron lft-model $N/R$ with $N_D\simeq Z$ inducing the identity on $G_F$. This supplies effective descent as a scheme, including its group law.

source.place: BLR 10.1 Proposition 7, printed p.293, point extension, Proposition 2, and descent

proof.text: The Néron property of $N$ applied to the smooth $R$-scheme $B$ extends the identity of generic fibres to $\beta:B\to N$. After base change to $D$, this is the chart $B_D\to Z$: both extend the same generic map and $Z$ has the injective Néron restriction map. It respects the group operations by that same uniqueness on $B\times_R B$, $B$ and $S$. By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-triples-presentation], $D$ is the colimit of the residue-triple diagram, so [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] makes $R\to D$ faithfully flat; its spectrum map is affine, hence quasi-compact, and $\{\operatorname{Spec}D\to S\}$ is an fpqc covering. By [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms](3) its pullback $\{N_D\to N\}$ is an fpqc covering of $N$, and $B\times_NN_D=B_D$. Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-descend-open-immersion] to $\beta$ and this covering, whose base change is the open chart, to conclude that $\beta$ is an open group immersion. Every geometric point of $S$ lifts through this cover. On each resulting geometric fibre step 3 identifies its image with the component containing the identity. Therefore the image of $\beta$ is exactly $N^0$. Finally the implication (i)$\Rightarrow$(ii) in [lem-sfb-neron-dvr-point-criterion] applied over $R$ gives the requested surjectivity for every essentially smooth local DVR extension $R\to A$.
